analysis: The changes to docs/developer/test.md are documentation only. The patch bumps the last-updated date, rewords the cluster runtime CI runner description to a link to build.md#ci-runner-routing, and reworks a CI routing check note near lines 1804-1810, which falls outside the supplied text units. I examined the supplied excerpts (lines 457-1385). They describe test procedures for the prefix cache (T-041), the App Attest endpoint-resumption tests (T-053), the add-on hold (TB-012, T-059, T-060), the watchdog, and native serving qualification. None of this changes code, wire contracts, keys, authorization or cache behavior. The text keeps the documented safety guidance: use isolated key namespaces, never use production cache roots or keys, and treat tests as non-qualifying for physical Apple or fleet rollout. The only security-adjacent change is a wording change on CI runners. Replacing 'Blacksmith' with generic 'macOS CI runners' for the cluster runtime tests, and the statement that release workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners, are descriptive. The actual workflow, routing script and build.md content are not supplied, so I cannot verify that the doc matches the real runner routing or that the release-signing workflow keeps its pinned runner. That is an unverified contract, not evidence of a regression. No findings, and no threat-model gap is introduced by this documentation edit.
